subject: series
synopsis: Stories in the style of Batman: The Animated Series, featuring the Dark Knight in adventures aimed at a younger audience.

subject: series
synopsis: Neal Adams's long-delayed and stylistically baffling return to Batman, featuring the artist's surreal, unparseable storytelling and obsessive attention to anatomical detail. Generally considered one of the most confusing superhero comics ever published, fascinating as artifact if not as narrative.
author: Neal Adams

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover miniseries bringing Bill Willingham's Bigby Wolf from Fables into Gotham City for a conflict with Batman. A fun genre clash that will appeal most to fans of both franchises.
author: Bill Willingham

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Rucka's six-issue limited series exploring Helena Bertinelli's origins and her violent methods, as Batman and Oracle investigate her past while she hunts the Mafia family that destroyed her own. Rucka writes the character with the same moral complexity he brings to all his DC work.
author: Greg Rucka

subject: series
synopsis: A Fear Itself aftermath mini-series that introduced Marcus Johnson, a soldier who discovers a shocking connection to Nick Fury, setting up the debut of the Marvel Cinematic Universe-inspired Nick Fury Jr. in the main comics continuity.
author: Chris Yost

subject: series
synopsis: Yann and Alain Henriet's Franco-Belgian WWII aviation drama: Silesian childhood friends, among them future test pilot Hanna Reitsch, drawn to opposite sides of the war.

subject: series
synopsis: Humorous animal-focused Infinity Comics

subject: series
synopsis: A comic series.

subject: series
synopsis: Tsutomu Nihei's post-apocalyptic manga follows Zoichi Kanoe and his AI motorcycle partner COmpany across a dying world infected with a transforming virus. Nihei's architectural scope and dense visual world-building create a uniquely oppressive atmosphere of machine-age desolation.
author: Tsutomu Nihei

subject: series
synopsis: Howard Chaykin and David Tischman's vampire mob drama follows a Miami crime family that discovers their patriarch was actually a vampire — leading to blood-soaked succession politics where undeath is just another form of power.
author: Howard Chaykin

subject: series
synopsis: A Heavy Metal series exploring dark atmosphere and mysterious narrative structures.

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Latour and Ivan Brandon's dark fantasy follows a woman who sells escape into tailored dreamworlds, until a powerful and dangerous client wants to take what she owns.
author: Jason Latour

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Wood and Garry Brown's Viking saga following Magnus the Black, a Christian warrior navigating a treacherous Northern European landscape. Wood's laconic scripts and Brown's atmospheric black-and-white art combine into a compelling historical adventure.
author: Brian Wood

subject: series
synopsis: A Blackest Night tie-in miniseries featuring the Flash and the Rogues as they face the Black Lantern versions of dead Rogues members.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: The 3-issue Blackest Night tie-in focuses on the Justice Society confronting Black Lantern versions of their dead colleagues, delivering character-specific emotional payoffs for the team with the deepest connection to heroic legacy and loss.
author: James Robinson

subject: series
synopsis: The 3-issue Blackest Night tie-in follows Diana's transformation into a Star Sapphire and her emotional conflict with a Black Lantern version of Maxwell Lord. Greg Rucka scripts and Nicola Scott draws, making this one of the stronger single-character tie-in minis of the event.
author: Greg Rucka

subject: series
synopsis: Juan Díaz Canales and Juanjo Guarnido's painted noir series about John Blacksad, a feline private eye in 1950s America, through cases of racism, the Red Scare and jazz-age decay.

subject: series
synopsis: A noir detective thriller set in a future where vampires and humans coexist uneasily, following a detective investigating a series of murders that threatens the fragile peace between the species. Stylish and violent, blending cyberpunk aesthetics with classic vampire mythology.
author: Eliot Rahal

subject: series
synopsis: Based on FromSoftware's gothic horror RPG, this comic series expands the lore of Yharnam and the Hunt. Atmospheric and deeply unsettling, it captures the game's Lovecraftian cosmic horror and bleak beauty.

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Seeley's Aftershock series about a corporation developing superhuman abilities that sells its products to the highest bidder, told from the perspective of an investigative journalist exposing the truth.
author: Tim Seeley

subject: series
synopsis: A new creator-owned adventure series from BOOM! Studios.

subject: series
synopsis: Action-packed Infinity Comics featuring enhanced characters

subject: series
synopsis: Kyle Higgins and Alec Siegel's alternate history series about a union of superheroes in 1960s Chicago negotiating their contracts while dealing with a new villain. The labor-politics premise is fresh; the period atmosphere is well-rendered.
author: Kyle Higgins, Alec Siegel

subject: series
synopsis: David Lapham's viscerally transgressive take on the Roman emperor Caligula, depicting his madness, cruelty, and depraved reign through explicit horror imagery and unflinching violence characteristic of Avatar's output.
author: David Lapham

subject: series
synopsis: David Lapham's sequel to his Caligula series, continuing the graphic depiction of Rome under the mad emperor's reign with extreme violence and decadence as Avatar's house aesthetic.
author: David Lapham

subject: series
synopsis: Larry Hama's tie-in comic set in the near-future world of Black Ops III, expanding on the game's transhuman soldiers and cyber-warfare themes. Competent military sci-fi with Hama's reliable action-comic craft, but limited outside the game's fanbase.
author: Larry Hama

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse continuation of the Canto fantasy series — following the small tin robot hero on new adventures in a darkly fairy-tale world — building on the character's established emotional resonance with accessible all-ages storytelling.
author: David M. Booher

subject: series
synopsis: David Morrell's intimate six-issue story presents a dying Steve Rogers projecting his spirit to guide a young soldier in Afghanistan, a surprisingly moving meditation on heroism and legacy divorced from Marvel continuity.
author: David Morrell

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker and Bryan Hitch's ambitious miniseries depicting Steve Rogers' return from his apparent death after Civil War, involving time-displacement and the Red Skull's scheme to possess his body; a landmark moment in the modern Captain America mythos.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn's arc following the partnership between Steve Rogers and Natasha Romanoff against a shadowy conspiracy, a solid espionage-tinged superhero story that leverages the natural chemistry between two of Marvel's most skilled operatives.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's revival of the classic Golden Age aviator hero, following the WWII-era superhero who is brought into the modern day and must adjust while battling the legacy of his old enemies. A capable retro superhero adventure with nostalgic appeal.
author: Joshua Williamson

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' superhero team series featuring Captain Paragon leading a team of heroes, part of AC's efforts to build a coherent universe of golden age-style costumed heroes in the 1980s.

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Casey's revival of Jack Kirby's post-Marvel creator-owned character Captain Victory, bringing Kirby's wild cosmic mythology back with contemporary storytelling and deep reverence for the source material.
author: Joe Casey

subject: series
synopsis: Akane Shimizu's charming educational manga anthropomorphizes the cells of the human body as workers in a city-sized organism, following a cheerful Red Blood Cell (erythrocyte) and a stoic White Blood Cell (neutrophil) through bacterial invasions and cellular crises. Surprisingly accurate and endlessly inventive.
author: Akane Shimizu

subject: series
synopsis: A revival of Chaos Comics' horror universe featuring Lady Death, Evil Ernie, and related characters in a dark horror event series published through Dynamite.

subject: series
synopsis: A Chaos War tie-in in which the chaos god's attack causes the dead to rise, temporarily resurrecting deceased Avengers including Yellowjacket, Captain Mar-Vell, and Doctor Druid for one final mission; a fun nostalgia piece for classic Avengers fans.
author: Fred Van Lente

subject: series
synopsis: Defiant Comics title starring a near-immortal soldier who has fought across centuries of human warfare, reimagined in the modern world. A historical-flavored action series tied into the Defiant shared universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Crime or horror thriller series from MadCave centering on investigations into fires, arson, or aftermath of catastrophic destruction.
author: Anthony Cleveland

subject: series
synopsis: Vincent Dugomier and Benoît Ers's series about three children in occupied France who start their own resistance against the German occupiers.

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis' continuation of Chronicles of Wormwood as the nice Antichrist Danny faces pressure to finally do his job.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: A comic adaptation of the NBC spy comedy series Chuck, following Chuck Bartowski's misadventures as an Intersect.
author: Rupe

subject: series
synopsis: Anthology of Hellraiser stories expanding Clive Barker's cenobite mythology, featuring rotating creative teams exploring the lore of the Lament Configuration and the Order of the Gash.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A Clive Barker property from Epic Comics with horror and supernatural themes.
author: Clive Barker

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Skroce writes and draws the Thing in a run of slugfest team-ups across the Marvel Universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Comico's black-and-white showcase anthology for new talent, remembered for the first appearance of Matt Wagner's Grendel in #2.

subject: series
synopsis: Troy Hickman's acclaimed anthology series set in a chain of superhero coffee shops, where heroes and villains come for neutral territory and human moments. Sharp, witty, and surprisingly moving — one of the best anthologies of its era.

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series by Chuck Dixon featuring Connor Hawke, the second Green Arrow, facing a mystical threat involving dragon's blood that enhances fighting abilities. Dixon brings his expertise with martial arts action to this story.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Ron Marz's six-issue cosmic anthology spotlights Marvel's stellar tier -- Thanos, Terrax, Silver Surfer, Jack of Hearts, Quasar, and Legacy/Genis-Vell -- in standalone stories establishing the mid-1990s cosmic landscape.
author: Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: Cosmic adventure Infinity Comics

subject: series
synopsis: A Wildstorm crossover event where The Authority seizes control of the United States government.
author: Ed Brubaker, Robbie Morrison, Micah Ian Wright, Chuck Austen

subject: series
synopsis: Image's rotating-creator horror anthology revives the Stephen King/George Romero franchise, delivering EC Comics-style supernatural comeuppance in short-form stories built for pure dread.

subject: series
synopsis: Guido Crepax's The Complete Crepax — the collected Italian erotic and psychedelic comics masterwork featuring Valentina, the photojournalist-adventurer who became one of the defining figures of European erotic comics.
author: Guido Crepax

subject: series
synopsis: Si Spurrier's arc of the Crossed +100 series, set a century after the Crossed apocalypse, examining the fragile remnants of human civilization through a linguistically inventive lens.
author: Si Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: Gail Simone and Cat Staggs' body-swap crime thriller pairs a Chicago hitman with a Seattle housewife; each inhabiting the other's world, they discover surprising competence and dangerous secrets.
author: Gail Simone

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Soule and Ryan Browne's anarchic fantasy comedy follows Wizord, a powerful mage dispatched from a hellish dimension to destroy Earth, who decides he likes it here far too much to follow orders.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: A one-shot special marking DC's 2024 publishing relaunch, setting up new directions for Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, and the wider DC universe. Written by Scott Snyder and Joshua Williamson, it serves as the entry point for DC's All In initiative.
author: Scott Snyder, Joshua Williamson

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series starring the Titans' Cyborg, Victor Stone's first solo mini.

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology series featuring wordless DC comics stories told entirely through art, with contributions from a variety of DC creators. The silent format challenges artists to convey narrative purely through visual storytelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue crossover limited series between DC Comics and WildStorm, in which a malevolent entity forces WildStorm's heroes to fight classic DC characters including the Justice League. Written by Keith Giffen with art by Lee Garbett.
author: Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid's acclaimed first volume of Daredevil; optimistic and character-focused humanist approach.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Justin Jordan's horror series for Avatar exploring ancient malevolent deities awakening in the modern world, blending cosmic horror with action in Avatar's typically transgressive mode.
author: Justin Jordan

subject: series
synopsis: Image's comic adaptation of EA's survival horror video game franchise, providing backstory for the Ishimura disaster and the Necromorph threat. A competent tie-in for fans of the game.
author: Antony Johnston

subject: series
synopsis: A five-issue limited series by Steve Vance revisiting Boston Brand's origins and his mission as the ghostly hero Deadman, balancing supernatural adventure with existential reflection on life and death.
author: Steve Vance

subject: series
synopsis: Carlo Barberi story in which Deadpool is framed for a bombing and hunted by Punisher, Daredevil, and Spider-Man while trying to clear his name.
author: Mike Benson

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Benson and Adam Glass reimagine Wade Wilson as a Cold War operative in 1950s McCarthyite America, delivering a clever genre mash-up that works better than expected by stripping away meta-humor in favour of genuine period noir.
author: Mike Benson

subject: series
synopsis: Action comedy featuring iconic rivals

subject: series
synopsis: An Ahoy Comics series exploring dark and comedic themes.

subject: series
synopsis: A Zenescope action-horror series featuring a protagonist wielding death-related supernatural powers, part of the publisher's mature superhero/fantasy line.

subject: series
synopsis: The sequel to Monty Nero and Mike Dowling's Death Sentence, continuing in a world where an STD grants extraordinary powers before killing the host, this arc moves the action to London with new characters and escalating societal collapse.

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Soule's follow-up to Death of Wolverine exploring the aftermath as Weapon X seeks new subjects to fill the void left by Logan's death.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: Comprehensive reprints of classic Doctor Strange/Defenders team stories.

subject: series
synopsis: Action-adventure series from MadCave based on or inspired by the classic animated Defenders of the Earth property featuring Flash Gordon, Mandrake the Magician, and The Phantom.
author: Dan DiDio

subject: series
synopsis: A collected volume reprinting the first five years of Tony Millionaire's Maakies newspaper strip, gathering the darkly comic misadventures of drunken sailor Drinky Crow and his companion Uncle Gabby.
author: Tony Millionaire

subject: series
synopsis: Omnibus collection of Jeff Lemire and Dustin Nguyen's acclaimed sci-fi series following robot TIM-21 across a robot-hostile galaxy.
author: Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman's story of an aging, terminal superhero called Destroyer who decides to take down as many supervillains as he can before he dies.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and John McCrea's irreverent, deliberately crude comedy series about two Belfast layabouts continues with apocalyptic irreverence, pushing bad taste humor to its extremes.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: A Disney comics series based on the animated Hercules franchise, featuring new adventures of the mythological hero in Disney's animated style.

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Cantwell and Salvador Larroca's nuanced solo series follows Victor Von Doom navigating a geopolitical crisis involving Victorious and Symkaria while wrestling with his own contradictions as both villain and reluctant hero.
author: Christopher Cantwell

subject: series
synopsis: Sara Barnes's MAX-imprint solo story follows the Squadron Supreme's Doctor Spectrum in an extended sci-fi meditation on power and alien consciousness, competently executed if tonally uneven.
author: Sara Barnes

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid's 2018 Doctor Strange run that reimagined the Sorcerer Supreme as a globe-trotting magical problem-solver after the events of his previous series, with Strange operating without his Sanctum Sanctorum and dealing with a depleted magical community. Features clever magical concepts and an adventurous tone.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Humorous dog superhero Infinity Comics

subject: series
synopsis: C.B. Cebulski and Sana Takeda's vampire horror series following an ancient Japanese vampire in modern-day San Francisco drawn into conflict with a new generation of predators. Takeda's gorgeous painterly art is the primary draw.
author: C.B. Cebulski

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Simon Coleby's beautifully understated WWII story about the Tuskegee Airmen — America's first Black fighter pilots — told in parallel between a combat veteran and his son during the Civil Rights era.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: A Wildstorm action series featuring dual protagonists navigating international intrigue and combat.
author: Josh Williamson

subject: series
synopsis: The third chapter of the Dune House prequel comic trilogy, adapting Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson's novels depicting the final decades before Paul Atreides is born.
author: Brian Herbert

subject: series
synopsis: The IDW adaptation of R.A. Salvatore's iconic Dark Elf trilogy follows Drizzt Do'Urden's origin in the Underdark, bringing the beloved novel series to comics for fans of the Forgotten Realms setting.
author: Andrew Dabb

subject: series
synopsis: A Zenescope series following villain protagonists or anti-heroes operating under the E.V.I.L. designation, exploring the darker side of the GFT universe from the antagonists' perspective.

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue anthology series set in the Arrowverse TV universe, featuring stories based on the CW DC shows including The Flash, Batwoman, Supergirl, and Green Arrow and the Canaries. Written by various TV show writers.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: The second anthology series from Ahoy's Poe line, presenting darkly comedic horror adaptations and pastiches of Poe's work alongside original macabre tales. Continues the tradition of literary horror humor.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse archival collection of Joe Kubert's acclaimed run on Tarzan (1972-1976) for DC Comics, widely regarded as one of the finest interpretations of Edgar Rice Burroughs' jungle hero, showcasing Kubert's masterful draftsmanship and storytelling.
author: Joe Kubert

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen's swashbuckling pirate adventure series set in the age of sail, following Capitan Donavan and a crew of rogues on the high seas. Brisk, fun, and visually lush — one of CrossGen's most accessible titles before the company's 2004 bankruptcy cut it short.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series introducing Chato Santana as the new El Diablo, a gangster who gains the power to channel a pyrokinetic demon and tries to use it to protect his community. Written by Jai Nitz with art by Phil Hester.
author: Jai Nitz

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series by Steve Orlando set in the far future of the DC universe, in which Earth's champions compete in a cosmic tournament to determine their planet's fate. A science fiction adventure expanding on DC's cosmic mythology.
author: Steve Orlando

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Carey and Salvador Larroca's five-issue Ultimate-universe mini: college student Elektra Natchios's first turn toward violence.

subject: series
synopsis: A continuation of the Elephantmen universe set in the year 2261, following the adventures of Theo Laroux and the hybrid soldiers of the Elephantmen. Richard Starkings' world of genetically engineered human-animal hybrids navigating a complex future society continues with new stories set in this well-developed sci-fi universe.
author: Richard Starkings

subject: series
synopsis: D.J. Kirkbride and Nikos Koutsis's sci-fi heist story set in a future where interplanetary couriers are hired for increasingly dangerous deliveries, following a veteran and a rookie navigating a job that quickly goes wrong. Fun space adventure.
author: D.J. Kirkbride

subject: series
synopsis: Sarah Vaughn and Jonathan Luna's Image series unfolds in a fractured land where two strangers on opposite sides of a brutal war discover they are mystically destined to found a new empire together. A slow-burn fantasy of duty, prophecy, and reluctant connection.
author: Sarah Vaughn

subject: series
synopsis: Accordion-era Valiant/Acclaim series following the immortal warrior brothers Gilad and Armstrong through the centuries — a continuation of the eternal warriors mythology.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A young man trapped in a monotonous afterlife purgatory begins to question his existence and soon discovers he has the power to change the fates of the damned around him.
author: Joshua Hale Fialkov

subject: series
synopsis: Ian Boothby and Gisèle Lagacé's supernatural comedy about two sisters — an exorcist and her demon-dealing sister — navigating Hell's bureaucracy and demonic commerce. Witty and well-drawn with a distinct comedic voice.
author: Ian Boothby

subject: series
synopsis: Jody Houser's Valiant series follows Faith Herbert, a plus-sized, pop-culture-obsessed fangirl who is also the superhero Zephyr — one of the most refreshing superhero protagonists of the 2010s. Celebrated for its joyful tone, genuine representation of a non-standard body type, and Houser's affectionate, funny scripts.
author: Jody Houser

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Carey and Jock's psychological thriller about a group of college students and a friend who appears from nowhere with no past, raising questions about memory, identity, and what makes someone real.
author: Mike Carey

subject: series
synopsis: A European fantasy or action series presenting a guard or soldier protagonist caught between duty and conscience in a morally compromised conflict — atmospheric and character-driven.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's landmark run is a sweeping, mathematically precise epic that expands the Fantastic Four mythos into civilizational-scale stakes involving the Future Foundation, the Council of Reeds, and the seeds of his later Avengers and Secret Wars work. Required reading.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Casey and Chris Weston's six-issue retelling of the Fantastic Four's origin adds psychological realism and retrofuturist texture to the classic story, exploring the team's first chaotic weeks after gaining their powers.
author: Joe Casey

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman and Cliff Rathburn's six-issue mini giving the Fantastic Four's villains the spotlight.

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips' genre-bending series fusing noir with Lovecraftian horror, following Josephine — a woman cursed with supernatural allure — across multiple decades as men destroy themselves for her while an ancient evil pursues her.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: Jorge Corona's all-ages fantasy about a feathered boy living in the gutter labyrinth beneath a walled city who befriends a girl from the privileged classes above. Beautiful art, a warm coming-of-age heart, and thoughtful class commentary wrapped in an accessible adventure.
author: Jorge Corona

subject: series
synopsis: A BOOM Studios horror miniseries following a family of illegal immigrants crossing the US-Mexico border who encounter supernatural predators in the desert. Uses genre horror to engage with real immigration anxieties and human desperation.
author: Swifty Lang

subject: series
synopsis: An early AC Comics publication featuring female-led content, part of the company's long history of publishing stories centered on female heroes and pin-up art.

subject: series
synopsis: A young man determined to become the best fencer in the country enrolls at a prestigious boarding school where he must navigate rivalry, class tensions, and his complicated feelings for his roommate.
author: C.S. Pacat

subject: series
synopsis: A collected volume of Trish Forano's Feral, a charming story about stray cats navigating the dangers of the outdoors, rendered in a beautifully expressive art style.
author: Tony Fleecs

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Wood and Denys Cowan's crime drama about an underground street fighter from Washington D.C. drawn into dangerous underground circuits that serve bigger criminal purposes.
author: Brian Wood

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and George Perez's epic tie-in to Final Crisis, uniting three different versions of the Legion of Super-Heroes across time to face Superboy-Prime and the Legion of Super-Villains, with massive implications for DC's future continuity.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Josh Lee Gordon's Firefly story set years later, following the next generation of the Serenity crew.
author: Josh Lee Gordon

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Kindt and Matt Smith's fairy-tale inversion follows a boy in a world of magic and fairy tales who dreams of the mythical place called the Real World — a clever deconstruction of genre expectations.
author: Matt Kindt

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue tie-in to the Forever Evil event in which the Flash's Rogues gallery—led by Captain Cold—refuse to join the Crime Syndicate's takeover and fight back against the villains terrorizing Central City. Written by Brian Buccellato with art by Patrick Zircher.
author: Brian Buccellato

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series reviving Jack Kirby's cosmic New Gods characters, the Forever People, following them in new adventures involving the Mother Box and the ongoing conflict between New Genesis and Apokolips.
author: Jack Kirby

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series by Keith Giffen and J.M. DeMatteis reuniting the classic bwahaha-era JLI cast including Booster Gold, Blue Beetle, Fire, and Mary Marvel in a comedic adventure. A warm and funny return to the beloved DeMatteis/Giffen partnership.
author: Keith Giffen, J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: Artbook celebrating the iconic artwork of Frank Thorne, the artist most associated with defining Red Sonja's visual identity in the 1970s.
author: Frank Thorne

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology celebrating contemporary romance comics across multiple stories, reviving the classic romance genre with modern sensibilities and diverse relationships.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Friday Fitzhugh returns to her hometown after her first semester at college, only to be dragged back into the supernatural mysteries she and her childhood best friend used to solve together.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: Claire Gibson, Marian Churchland, and Ryan Kelly's political fantasy following multiple characters in a feudal world as power shifts and alliances fracture across competing noble houses and their subjects. Deliberately paced and character-driven with rich world-building.
author: Claire Gibson

subject: series
synopsis: Bob Fingerman's semi-autobiographical post-apocalyptic satire: the cartoonist and his wife wander a nuked New York.

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics humor/adventure reprint series

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Darick Robertson's WWII Nick Fury: a young Sergeant Fury fights from North Africa into Germany in Ennis's unsentimental war-comic mode.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW crossover collection featuring stories of the G.I. Joe team working alongside the Autobots against their combined enemies.

subject: series
synopsis: The Sigma 6 era G.I. Joe comics following the animated series continuity, adapting the redesigned team's adventures for readers of the accompanying cartoon. Licensed tie-in material primarily for fans of the Sigma 6 animated show.

subject: series
synopsis: A collection of Gabrielle Bell's short diary comics originally published online, capturing the texture of daily life with the quiet intensity and wry self-observation that distinguished her as one of the best autobiographical cartoonists of her generation. Essential for readers who came to Bell through Lucky or Cecil and Jordan.
author: Gabrielle Bell

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Lobdell's six-issue X-Men spinoff strands Gambit and Bishop together across time following the events of the Magneto War, delivering serviceable X-Men adventure without particularly distinguishing itself.
author: Scott Lobdell

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Weisman's prequel series set in 10th-century Scotland following the gargoyle clan.
author: Greg Weisman

subject: series
synopsis: A WildStorm tie-in series to the Gen13 line featuring young heroes with Gen-Factor powers navigating action-adventure scenarios; a companion title to the main Gen13 series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's omnibus editions of the 1990s Ghost series: Elisa Cameron, a murdered reporter returned as an armed spirit, hunting her killers in Arcadia.
author: Remy Lai

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Clayton Crain's haunting Civil War-era Ghost Rider story follows a Confederate soldier whose encounter with a spirit rider in the 1860s echoes into a confrontation with modern evil. Crain's painterly digital art gives it an eerie, genuinely elegiac atmosphere.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Masterworks collection of classic Ghost Rider stories. Excellent exploration of supernatural antihero themes.

subject: series
synopsis: Howard Mackie's early-1990s series teams Johnny Blaze and Danny Ketch as twin spirits of vengeance, serving as a crossover companion to the main Ghost Rider ongoing through the Maximum Carnage and other 90s events.
author: Howard Mackie

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's fiery conclusion to his Ghost Rider run pits Johnny Blaze and Danny Ketch against an Antichrist scheme, delivering relentless supernatural action with genuine theological stakes and Roland Boschi's visceral art.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: Jamie Delano's Vertigo series connecting Native American spiritual traditions with contemporary urban violence, part of Delano's post-Hellblazer work exploring shamanism and primal mythology.
author: Jamie Delano

subject: series
synopsis: Bronze Age giant-sized specials featuring Marvel's non-team of Hulk, Doctor Strange, and Namor (later Silver Surfer) in extra-length adventures that expanded on the monthly Defenders series and showcased the team's distinctive anything-goes approach to superhero storytelling.
author: Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: Tsukumizu's minimalist masterpiece following two girls, Chito and Yuuri, wandering an abandoned post-apocalyptic city in a military vehicle, foraging for food and contemplating the remnants of human civilization. Deeply melancholic and quietly philosophical, with spare art that makes the emptiness feel enormous.
author: Tsukumizu

subject: series
synopsis: Zoe Quinn and Robbi Rodriguez's cyberpunk thriller follows a programmer who discovers her dead mother's hacker legacy and a conspiracy buried inside the world's dominant AI network — urgent, cyberfeminist, and visually electric.
author: Zoe Quinn

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Mowry's long-running IDW Godzilla series pits the King of Monsters against a rotating cast of kaiju in a military-political framework, delivering reliable monster-battle entertainment for Toho fans.
author: Chris Mowry

subject: series
synopsis: Collected editions reprinting IDW's celebrated Godzilla comic series and miniseries for new readers.

subject: series
synopsis: Jacob Semahn and Jorge Corona's story about the Latimer siblings who are thrust into supernatural danger when their monster-hunting parents are killed, forced to use their parents' arsenal to survive. A fun adventure with strong sibling dynamics.
author: Jacob Semahn

subject: series
synopsis: Police procedural drama set in Gotham City following non-powered law enforcement.
author: Greg Rucka

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Seeley and Tom King's espionage series following Dick Grayson as a spy for the organization Spyral, combining superhero adventure with James Bond-style intrigue after his identity was exposed.
author: Tim Seeley, Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: Anthology of Green Lantern stories featuring the full Corps across the universe.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hal Jordan and Barry Allen team up in this two-part crossover miniseries.
author: Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: This six-issue prestige mini-series retells Hal Jordan's origin story, showing his transformation from a reckless test pilot into Earth's Green Lantern after discovering a dying alien.
